source.english_context: Unit 01 Arrival and First Week Goal: arrive safely, answer basic questions, and get through the first days without panic. Daily Life English I just arrived in the United States. I am staying at this address. Can you please speak slowly? I need help finding my ride. Where is baggage claim? My suitcase has not arrived. Where can I get a luggage cart? Is there free Wi-Fi here? Where can I exchange money? How do I get to the train station? Could you write the address for me? My flight arrived late. Where is the information desk? I am looking for the airport shuttle. May I use your phone to call my host? Vocabulary arrival the time when you get to a place address the place where you live or stay customs the airport check for people and bags baggage claim the place where you get your bags ride a car trip from one place to another emergency contact a person to call if you need help luggage bags and suitcases used when traveling terminal a building at an airport where passengers arrive and leave shuttle a vehicle that makes short trips between places information desk a place where staff answer visitors' questions currency exchange a service that changes one country's money into another's host a person who welcomes you into their home US Customs People may ask direct questions. Short, clear answers are normal. Keep your passport, visa papers, address, and school or work information easy to reach. At the airport, ask staff for help if you are lost. Use simple sentences. At a service counter, wait for your turn and leave space for the person who is speaking with staff. Ask someone to repeat an unfamiliar place name, and check the spelling before following directions or booking a ride. Keep your destination written clearly, including the apartment number. Showing it can help when street names sound similar. Before leaving an information desk, repeat the terminal, exit, or meeting point to check that you understood correctly. Dialogue Officer: Where will you stay in the US? Student: I will stay at 125 Oak Street, Apartment 3B. Officer: What is the purpose of your trip? Student: I am here to study English. Officer: Which school will you attend? Student: Could you please repeat that slowly? Officer: What is the name of your school? Student: Oak Street English School. Here is the address. Officer: Thank you. Is that also your school contact number? Student: Yes, it is. I have it written here.

japanese_explanation.heading: 到着後すぐに必要な英語
points: 空港や駅では、短く正直に答えることが大切です。滞在先の住所、学校名、勤務先、緊急連絡先をすぐ見せられるようにしましょう。
聞き取れないときに、ゆっくり話してほしいと頼むのは失礼ではありません。低いレベルの学習者でも使える安全な表現です。
最初の一週間は、移動方法、携帯電話、家の鍵、近くのスーパー、緊急連絡先を先に確認すると安心です。

existing_simplified_chinese.heading: 刚到美国时最需要的英语
points: 在机场或车站，回答要简短、真实。把住宿地址、学校或工作信息、紧急联系人准备好，方便马上出示。
听不懂时，请对方说慢一点并不失礼。这是低级别学习者也可以放心使用的表达。
第一周先确认交通方式、手机、钥匙、附近超市和紧急联系人，这样生活会稳定很多。

ko.heading: 도착 후 바로 필요한 영어
points: 공항이나 역에서는 짧고 솔직하게 대답하는 것이 중요합니다. 숙소 주소, 학교 또는 직장 정보, 긴급 연락처를 즉시 보여줄 수 있도록 준비해 두세요.
못 알아들을 때 천천히 말해 달라고 부탁하는 것은 실례가 아닙니다. 초급 학습자도 안심하고 사용할 수 있는 표현입니다.
첫 일주일 동안은 이동 방법, 휴대폰, 집 열쇠, 가까운 슈퍼마켓, 긴급 연락처를 미리 확인해 두면 안심할 수 있습니다.

points: 在机场或车站，回答要简短、真实。把住宿地址、学校或工作信息、紧急联系人准备好，方便马上出示。

第一周先确认交通方式、手机、钥匙、附近超市和紧急联系人，这样生活会稳定很多。

es.heading: Inglés esencial justo después de llegar
points: En aeropuertos o estaciones, es importante responder de forma breve y honesta. Tenga lista la dirección de su estancia, la información de su escuela o trabajo y los contactos de emergencia para poder mostrarlos de inmediato.
Si no entiende, no es de mala educación pedir que le hablen más despacio. Incluso quienes están empezando a aprender inglés pueden usar esta expresión con confianza.
Durante la primera semana, le dará tranquilidad si verifica con antelación los métodos de transporte, el teléfono móvil, las llaves de casa, los supermercados cercanos y los contactos de emergencia.

pt-BR.heading: Inglês essencial logo após a chegada
points: Em aeroportos e estações, é importante responder de forma breve e honesta. Tenha o endereço de onde você vai ficar, as informações da sua escola ou trabalho e seus contatos de emergência prontos para mostrar imediatamente.
Quando você não entender, pedir para a pessoa falar devagar não é falta de educação. É uma expressão segura que até mesmo estudantes de nível básico podem usar.

Na primeira semana, você se sentirá mais tranquilo se verificar com antecedência os métodos de transporte, o telefone celular, as chaves de casa, os supermercados próximos e os contatos de emergência.

fr.heading: Anglais essentiel juste après l'arrivée
points: Dans les aéroports et les gares, il est important de répondre brièvement et honnêtement. Ayez l'adresse de votre lieu de séjour, les informations de votre école ou de votre travail et vos contacts d'urgence à portée de main pour les montrer immédiatement.
Si vous ne comprenez pas, il n’est pas impoli de demander à la personne de parler plus lentement. Même les débutants peuvent utiliser cette formule sans crainte d’être impolis.

Pendant la première semaine, vous vous sentirez plus en sécurité si vous vérifiez à l'avance les modes de transport, le téléphone portable, les clés de la maison, les supermarchés proches et les contacts d'urgence.

de.heading: Wichtiges Englisch direkt nach der Ankunft
points: An Flughäfen oder Bahnhöfen ist es wichtig, kurz und ehrlich zu antworten. Halten Sie die Adresse Ihres Aufenthaltsortes, Ihre Schul- oder Arbeitsinformationen und Ihre Notfallkontakte bereit, um sie sofort zeigen zu können.
Wenn Sie etwas nicht verstehen, ist es nicht unhöflich, um langsameres Sprechen zu bitten. Auch wer gerade erst Englisch lernt, kann diese Formulierung bedenkenlos verwenden.
Für die erste Woche ist es beruhigend, die Transportmittel, das Mobiltelefon, die Hausschlüssel, nahegelegene Supermärkte und Notfallkontakte im Voraus zu überprüfen.
